chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) left Mecca one day before the Tarwiyah (the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah). So 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr accompanied him and said, 'O Abu Abdillah! The season of Hajj has arrived, yet you leave it and go to Iraq?' He replied, 'O son of al-Zubayr! To be buried by the shore of the Euphrates is more beloved to me than to be buried in the courtyard of the Ka'bah.'

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, when pilgrims would fill their water skins before proceeding to Mina.
key_terms.شَاطِئِ الْفُرَاتِ: The shore of the Euphrates River, referring to the region of Karbala.
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ: A prominent companion and leader who accompanied Imam al-Husayn during his departure.
key_terms.فِنَاءِ الْكَعْبَةِ: The courtyard of the Ka'bah in Mecca.

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Husayn prefer to be buried by the Euphrates rather than in Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights Imam al-Husayn’s conscious departure from the Hajj rituals to fulfill his divine mission, emphasizing that his martyrdom at Karbala holds greater spiritual weight than the sanctity of Mecca itself. The preference for the banks of the Euphrates over the Ka'bah's courtyard underscores the theological concept of *fada'il* (virtues) where specific locations gain sanctity through the sacrifice of the Ahl al-Bayt, a key theme in Shia devotional geography.
